plan.title: Plant hall café — ground floor plan, 1:100
plan.aria: Plan of the café: the counter along the brick wall, the stair to the mezzanine on the back wall, tables to the east and planters inside the door.

copy.name: Café
diary: Week 1 · Measured survey
Counter on the brick wall, so the queue forms along it and not across the door. The stair stays where it is.
Week 2 · Concept
Drawn from the door: the trusses, the steel stair, a ceiling of plants to walk in under.
Week 4 · Strip-out and making good
Brick cleaned back, trusses painted, the mezzanine made safe. Everything stays white until it’s decided.
Weeks 6–9 · Joinery and FF&E
The steel stair goes in first, then the counter and the bench. Planters next, and the tables work round them.
Weeks 10–11 · Floor, brick, paint
Screed polished, brick sealed, walls in a warm white that holds the morning light. Beech tops, a pine counter.
Week 12 · Lighting and commissioning
Bare lamps on long flex at 2,700 K. 300 lux on the counter, softer everywhere else.
Day one · 08:00
Doors at eight. The queue moves.

end.title: Café
end.label: Take the corner table
end.aria: Go into the café and sit at the corner table

plan.title: Colonnade dining room — ground floor plan, 1:100
plan.aria: Plan of the dining room: booths along the blind wall, an arcade on three columns, tables by the windows on two sides and the bar at the back.

copy.name: Restaurant
diary: Week 1 · Measured survey
An arcade down the middle, glass on two sides. Booths go on the blind wall; the tables take the light.
Week 2 · Concept
Seen from under the arches, the way a guest first sees the room.
Week 5 · Plaster and making good
Ceiling roses restored, arches re-run in lime plaster, columns stripped back to the iron.
Weeks 7–10 · Booths, tables, the station
Booths on the blind wall. The service station sits behind the column, so the floor team never crosses the room.
Weeks 11–12 · Floors and panelling
Boards sanded and oiled dark, walnut on the booth wall, green leather on the booths, the shopfront reglazed.
Week 13 · Lighting
Opal globes at 2,700 K for the evening. By day the windows do the work.
First service · 12:00
Full but calm by two, and every seat faces something worth looking at.

plan.title: Back-bar — ground floor plan, 1:100
plan.aria: Plan of the bar: one long counter with the back-bar on the wall behind it, stools along the front, low tables and a banquette by the door.

copy.name: Bar
diary: Week 1 · Measured survey
One long counter, the back-bar on the wall behind it, a speed rail at every station.
Week 2 · Concept
Drawn from a stool. The back-bar is the stage; the counter is the front row.
Week 4 · Carcass
Counter framed in steel, the back-bar wall lined and levelled, the ceiling battened out.
Weeks 6–8 · Back-bar and stools
The back-bar shelves go up, three pendants are hung, and three stools are set at 750 mm.
Weeks 9–10 · Veneers and stone
Walnut on the front and across the ceiling, a honed marble top that takes a knock, green velvet on the stools.
Week 11 · Scenes
Three blown-glass pendants, a red wash over the corner, the back-bar at 40 lux. Nothing brighter than the bottles.
Opening night · 23:00
The light drops, the bottles glow, the counter fills.

plan.title: Atelier — ground floor plan, 1:100
plan.aria: Plan of the shop: a rail along the left wall, three fitting rooms with curtains in the back corner, a leaning mirror and planters in the middle, and the counter by the door.

copy.name: Shop
copy.intro: Scroll, and the shop builds itself: the plan, the sketch, the shell, the joinery, the finishes, the lights. A shop at eleven in the morning. One team from the first drawing to the first sale.
copy.srSummary: The build: a shop shown in seven stages, from the first drawing to opening day, with a short note from the studio at each stage. At the end you can see our shops or start a project. You can skip the build at any time.
diary: Week 1 · Measured survey
A white box with an arch. The rail takes the long wall; the fitting rooms go in the back corner, away from the door.
Week 2 · Concept
Drawn from the door, the way a customer first sees the room: the rail, the arch, the curtains at the back.
Week 3 · Partitions and making good
Fitting-room walls framed and boarded, the arch re-plastered, the ceiling made good for the new panels.
Weeks 5–7 · Joinery and fixtures
The brass rail, the mirror and the curtain tracks go up. Planters and a chair are set out round them.
Weeks 8–9 · Paint, floor, fabric
Terracotta in the fitting rooms, warm white everywhere else, a lilac resin floor and linen curtains to the ground.
Week 10 · Lighting
Flat panels at 3,000 K and 500 lux on the rail, so the colour you see is the colour you take home.
Opening day · 11:00
Doors at eleven. Everything on the rail is within reach, and every fitting room has a mirror.
